messages:
jia: Heads-up from Support: starting ~11:15 UTC multiple customers hit intermittent 502/504s and long timeouts against hosted inference. Major ones: brightmart, petitionlabs. Tickets: #6211, #6214.

olivia: Thanks. Opening incident channel — we need rapid containment then RCA. @matt can you look at gateway metrics?

matt: On it. Seeing a sharp rise in upstream 502s and a spike in active connections to runtime pool. NLB showing connection resets 11:14–11:17. p95 gateway latency climbed from 180ms -> ~1.2s.

sasha: Runtime side: a subset of model hosts in us-east-2 reporting KV latency spikes and occasional runtime worker GC stalls. Example log: ```2026-06-07T11:15:22Z runtime host-27 WARN kv_lookup latency=624ms key=ctx-*.```. Also GPUs on those nodes are near-saturated for a specific model variant.

jia: Impact notes from CS: customers see 504s on streaming and non-streaming endpoints; retries flood makes situation worse. We'll ask them to pause retries for now.

olivia: Immediate mitigation ideas: (A) split heavy-sequence traffic to fallback quantized variant, (B) raise gateway conn pool and reduce per-conn keepalive, (C) rate-limit large streaming/batched requests per-tenant. Who can implement A/B now?

matt: I'll apply pool changes and per-route rate limit. Rolling canary now.

deploy-bot: deploy started (matt): gateway/conn-tune v2026.06.07-11:22 — canary -> 10% -> 100%.

sasha: I'll prepare an on-host runtime patch: disable expensive KV write path and restart affected runtime worker group gracefully. Will target 3 hosts first.

matt: Canary done 11:26 UTC. Active connections reduced ~35%. p95 down to ~420ms but some 502s persist.

tim: CS update: sent interim message to impacted customers explaining mitigation and requesting clients to back off retries. Added support doc link.
\oljia: (typo) ignore

olivia: sasha — can you collect heap, KV histograms, and the exact request patterns from the tenant bursts? jia — gather sample request IDs from customers.

sasha: Collected heap and KV metrics; early correlation: one tenant ran a large streaming batch job at ~11:13 that produced many long-lived contexts and heated KV cache warmups. That plus runtime warm starts caused heavy KV write contention.

jia: Uploaded request IDs and sample payload sizes into #support-artifacts. Noted repeated long-context sequences from petitionlabs.

matt: Observed that the tenant's traffic used keepalive streams with slow client-side backoff. Combined with connection reuse we saw head-of-line effects.

olivia: Action list (short-term):
- olivia: coordinate comms and severity (ETA 11:35)
- matt: keep gateway pool change and keep per-route rate limiting in place; add temporary per-tenant streaming cap (ETA 11:40)
- sasha: patch runtime hotfix on affected hosts and run smoke harness (ETA 12:00)
- jia: liaise with customers to pause/reduce retries and batch sizes (ETA 11:45)
- anna: start postmortem doc + timeline capture (ETA EOD)

anna: noted — will own postmortem. Scheduling RCA for tomorrow.

sasha: Hotfix applied to 3 hosts at 11:48: disabled heavy KV write coalescing and restarted workers gracefully. CPU and KV latencies on those hosts dropped within 90s.

matt: After fixes, 5xx rate fell from ~7% -> 0.8% in ~10 minutes. p95 latency back to ~260ms. Remaining 504s mostly related to client retries/higher than normal inflight.

eng-sre-bot: Alert cleared: kv_latency_alarm us-east-2 cleared at 11:58:12 UTC.

jia: Customers confirm improved performance; one large customer still sees occasional 504s — CS is coordinating a follow-up call.

olivia: Great work. We'll hand off to oncall for continued monitoring. Keep thread for postmortem notes.

sasha: Running smoke test that simulates long-stream batches — pre-fix error 2.8%, post-fix 0.6%. Uploading artifacts.

matt: Post-incident action items (owners + notes):
- root cause: warmup + KV write contention + tenant burst pattern (sasha)
- infra: add per-tenant streaming rate caps and connection pool auto-scale (matt + eng-sre)
- SDK/client guidance: publish retry/backoff and recommended max batch size (jia + tim)
- monitoring: KV miss ratio, long-seqlen alarm, and tenant sudden-burst detection (olivia + eng-sre)
- runtime: evaluate KV write-path optimizations and safer warmup ramp (sasha)

tim: I'll set up customer remediation calls and track SLAs for affected tenants.

olivia: Scheduling postmortem 14:00 UTC tomorrow. Please add any additional notes to the doc link: https://redwood.internal/pm/postmortems/1769412345

anna: I'll compile timeline, impact table, mitigations, and owners with target dates.

sasha: All artifact links uploaded to #incidents-artifacts.

matt: I'll draft a short RFC for per-tenant circuit breakers and pool autoscaling.

olivia: Closing active response; leaving monitoring and follow-ups in this thread. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
